past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: In a clinical thermometer, mercury does NOT fall back to the bulb because
options: A. it is less in quantity.
B. it is in a capillary tube.
C. of the shape of the thermometer’s bulb.
D. of the constriction in the capillary tube.
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: A clinical thermometer has a narrow constriction just above the bulb. When the temperature rises, mercury expands and pushes past the constriction. When removed from the body, the column breaks at the constriction, preventing the mercury from flowing back, allowing accurate reading of the maximum temperature.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: The escape of high kinetic energy molecules in the form of vapours from the surface of a liquid without heating is known as
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: Evaporation is the surface phenomenon where molecules with higher kinetic energy escape from the surface of a liquid at any temperature without requiring the liquid to boil.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: If an inflated tyre of a car bursts, then the temperature of air that will escape from the tyre
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: When a tyre bursts, the escaping air undergoes rapid adiabatic expansion. According to thermodynamics, rapid expansion causes work to be done by the gas at the expense of its internal energy, resulting in a drop in temperature.
